newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol airport cargo volume to grow on back of KLM.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol airport cargo volume to grow on back of KLM.

text.p: The recent recovery in KLM's cargo fortunes in the second half of last year is likely to continue and should contribute a forecast growth in volume at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, the airport's cargo director said.

"Looking at the cargo carriers: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV has had a very difficult year but it made a good recovery in the latter half and I believe it will contribute more to the airport's (forecast) growth figure of seven per cent volume growth than it did last year," Fritz Bisschop told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
"I think the air cargo industry is becoming more competitive because of pressure on rates, and you will see certain shipments coming back from sea-to-air," he added.
Bisschop said today's global economic indicators led him to expect global trade to continue to grow and the air freight sector can expect to benefit.

"On the other hand its difficult to forecast market growth; my feeling is that 1997 will be a rather good year, but not entirely special. There are, after all, no indications of a boom, but I think we can expect a good 1997 in terms of air cargo volume," he stated.

Asked about the prospects for new business for the leading Dutch airport, Bisshop said: "If you look at the number of airlines in the Asia Pacific, almost all airlines operating with freighters have connections to Schiphol."
"Domestic carriers will increase their frequencies and international carriers will contribute to further growth.

However, I'm not expecting entire new airlines to switch hubs or to suddenly initiate large scale operations out of Schiphol this year, he added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
